run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three indices exist in Elasticsearch and were queried. (1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` field (mapping: @timestamp date, message text, service keyword, severity keyword); `term level=ERROR` returned 0 both in the default 1-hour window and across the full authorized window, and the correct field query `term severity=ERROR` returned 10. (2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` field either (mapping: @timestamp date, msg text, severity_num integer, svc keyword); `terms level=[ERROR,FATAL]` returned 0 in both windows, and the severity is numeric, so `terms severity_num=[5,6]` returned 8, made up of severity_num=5 (6 docs, msg tagged [ERROR]) plus severity_num=6 (2 docs, msg tagged [FATAL]). (3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no date-mapped field at all (mapping: ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text), so the @timestamp range did not error but matched nothing (0) and the tool reported no time filter was applied; filtering `ingest_ts` (keyword, ISO-8601 strings) to today 2026-11-23 UTC with `term level=ERROR` returned 7. All counts are index-level totals observed at query time; the exact document set can change after the query.

claims.text: Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); there is no `level` field in the mapping.
Query {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 in the default 1-hour window (2026-11-23T18:38:24Z–19:38:24Z).

Re-running the same {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 over the full authorized window 2026-10-24T19:38:24Z–2026-11-23T19:38:24Z also returned total 0, so the zero is not only a window effect.
On app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 the correct field query {"term":{"severity":"ERROR"}} over the full authorized window returned total 10.

On app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, match_all over the full authorized window totalled 16 documents with severity terms buckets ERROR=10 and INFO=6 and a single service bucket checkout-280=16, consistent with the severity=ERROR count of 10.
Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); there is no `level` field and no string severity field in the mapping.
Query {"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}} on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 0 in the default 1-hour window and also 0 over the full authorized window.
On app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the numeric severity query {"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}} over the full authorized window returned total 8.
On app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, match_all over the full authorized window totalled 13 documents with severity_num buckets 5=6, 3=5, 6=2, so 5 and 6 together account for exactly the 8 matched above.

Documents in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 show the severity_num encoding: severity_num=5 with msg "[ERROR] DB timeout N", severity_num=6 with msg "[FATAL] Disk full N", severity_num=3 with msg "[INFO] healthcheck N", all svc order-280, timestamps 2026-11-23T19:35:01Z–19:37:05Z.

Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text) only; no field in the mapping has type date, and the tool reported "No matched index maps a date field, so no time filter was applied".

On app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the request as asked (range on @timestamp for 2026-11-23T00:00:00Z–2026-11-24T00:00:00Z plus term level=ERROR) did not error but returned total 0, because @timestamp is not a mapped field in that index.
On app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 the corrected query range on ingest_ts (gte 2026-11-23T00:00:00, lt 2026-11-24T00:00:00) combined with term level=ERROR returned total 7.
On app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, match_all totalled 16 documents with level buckets ERROR=12 and INFO=4, so 7 of the 12 ERROR documents fall on 2026-11-23.

Documents in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 carry ingest_ts as un-zoned ISO-8601 strings such as "2026-11-23T08:01:00" and "2026-11-22T08:05:00" with level ERROR, and "2026-11-23T09:01:00" with level INFO; the sampled 16 documents contain 7 ERROR rows dated 2026-11-23 and 5 ERROR rows dated 2026-11-22.
The three indices app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 (16 docs), app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (13 docs) and app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 (16 docs) all exist, are health green and open at query time 2026-11-23T19:38:27Z.

The zero results for the originally-worded queries were caused by schema mismatch, not by absence of log entries: index a and b have no `level` field (a uses severity keyword, b uses integer severity_num) and index c has no date-typed field, so ingest_ts keyed lexicographically had to be used.

The documents in app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 appear to be timestamped around 2026-11-03T23:35Z–23:36Z (the source range reported by the full-window query), which would additionally explain why a default 1-hour-window query on that index matched nothing regardless of field name; the exact per-document timestamp spread was not read.

gaps: "Today" was interpreted as 2026-11-23 UTC from the run's reference time 2026-11-23T19:38:24Z; if a different timezone was intended for index c the answer of 7 would shift.
ingest_ts in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 is mapped as keyword and stored without a timezone, so the today-range was a lexicographic string comparison, not a date comparison.
Document counts are the state at query time (2026-11-23T19:38Z); documents indexed after the query are not covered, and index_stats/refresh behaviour was not examined.
For index a the per-document @timestamp values were not read (size=0 aggregations only); the Nov 3 timestamp is taken from the backend-reported source range.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this run, so why these logs were written (deployment or configuration chronology) could not be checked.
next_steps: If these indices are queried repeatedly, standardise the schema: use a single keyword severity/level field and one date-typed timestamp field across a, b and c.
Confirm the intended reporting timezone for index c's ingest_ts before publishing the count of 7 ERROR entries for 2026-11-23.
If the log contents are to be used as incident evidence, re-run against a mapping-aware query template and record the timestamp of each count.
